name: Whey protein isolate
benefits: Can help fill a dietary protein shortfall. Milk-derived; not necessary if food already meets your needs.
safety: Milk allergy; products can contain residual lactose.
how: Use the label’s serving size to fill a measured protein shortfall.

name: Whey protein concentrate
benefits: A convenient milk-protein source; protein and lactose content vary by product.
safety: Milk allergy and lactose intolerance.
how: Use the label’s serving size to fill a measured protein shortfall.

name: Hydrolyzed whey protein
benefits: Partially broken-down whey; no need to choose it over other complete proteins for most people.
safety: Milk allergy; premium prices do not guarantee better outcomes.
how: Use the label’s serving size to fill a measured protein shortfall.

name: Casein protein
benefits: A slower-digested milk protein that can contribute to total daily protein.
safety: Milk allergy and product-specific lactose content.
how: Use the label’s serving size to fill a measured protein shortfall.

name: Soy protein isolate
benefits: A plant-based complete protein option.
safety: Soy allergy; check label and medication timing with a pharmacist.
how: Use the label’s serving size to fill a measured protein shortfall.

name: Pea protein
benefits: A plant protein option; combine varied food proteins across the day.
safety: Legume allergies; protein content varies.
how: Use the label’s serving size to fill a measured protein shortfall.

name: Rice protein
benefits: A plant protein option, often blended with pea protein.
safety: Choose independently tested products; amino-acid balance varies.
how: Use the label’s serving size to fill a measured protein shortfall.

name: Plant protein blend
benefits: Blended plant proteins can help meet a protein target.
safety: Check all ingredient allergens and third-party testing.
how: Use the label’s serving size to fill a measured protein shortfall.

name: Ready-to-drink protein
benefits: Convenient when a meal or snack is impractical.
safety: Check added sugar, allergens and actual serving size.
how: Use the label’s serving size to fill a measured protein shortfall.

name: Protein bar
benefits: A portable snack; compare energy and protein on the label.
safety: Sugar alcohols may cause gastrointestinal symptoms.
how: Use the label’s serving size to fill a measured protein shortfall.

name: Creatine monohydrate
benefits: Can improve performance in repeated high-intensity effort and support training adaptations.
safety: Can increase body weight through water retention; discuss use with a clinician if you have kidney disease.
how: Many adult protocols use 3–5 g daily; loading is not required. Confirm suitability first.

name: Mass gainer
benefits: Adds calories and protein when ordinary food is insufficient.
safety: Large portions can overshoot calorie needs or cause digestive discomfort.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: Multivitamin / mineral
benefits: May help cover specific dietary gaps; not automatically needed by everyone.
safety: Avoid doubling up nutrients; vitamin K can interact with warfarin.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: Omega-3 fish oil
benefits: Supplies EPA and DHA when dietary sources are limited.
safety: Discuss anticoagulants, bleeding risk and high doses with a clinician.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: Algal omega-3
benefits: A non-fish source of DHA and sometimes EPA.
safety: Check actual EPA/DHA amounts; interactions depend on dose.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: Vitamin D
benefits: Useful when intake or vitamin D status is inadequate.
safety: Excess intake can cause hypercalcemia; do not self-prescribe high doses.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: Vitamin B12
benefits: Important for people with low intake or absorption; often relevant to vegan diets.
safety: Address the cause of deficiency with a clinician.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: Iron
benefits: Treats confirmed iron deficiency under appropriate guidance.
safety: Overdose is dangerous, especially for children; interacts with several medicines.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: Calcium
benefits: Can fill a calcium intake gap when food is insufficient.
safety: Can interfere with thyroid medication and some antibiotics.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: Magnesium
benefits: Corrects inadequate intake; extra magnesium is not a universal performance aid.
safety: Can cause diarrhea; kidney disease increases risk.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: Zinc
benefits: Useful for inadequate zinc intake.
safety: Long-term excess can cause copper deficiency; interacts with some antibiotics.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: ZMA blend
benefits: A zinc, magnesium and B6 mixture; no reliable blanket muscle-gain benefit.
safety: Avoid high combined nutrient doses from multiple supplements.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: Beta-alanine
benefits: May help some repeated high-intensity exercise lasting roughly 1–4 minutes.
safety: Can cause tingling; suitability and dose depend on the athlete.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: Caffeine
benefits: May improve alertness and some exercise performance; not a required fat-loss aid.
safety: Can cause anxiety, insomnia and rapid heart rate; count all caffeine sources and review stimulant interactions.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: Citrulline malate
benefits: Evidence for strength and performance outcomes remains mixed.
safety: Can cause digestive symptoms; review blood-pressure medicines with a clinician.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: BCAAs
benefits: Usually unnecessary when enough complete dietary protein is consumed.
safety: Not a replacement for a complete protein source.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: Glutamine
benefits: No consistent muscle-building or performance benefit in healthy exercisers.
safety: Discuss use in the context of liver, kidney or other medical conditions.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: Collagen peptides
benefits: Studied for connective-tissue outcomes; not a complete muscle-building protein.
safety: Animal-source allergies; does not replace complete dietary protein.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: CLA
benefits: Reported weight effects are small and inconsistent; not a first-line fat-loss strategy.
safety: May affect glucose regulation and cause digestive symptoms.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: L-carnitine
benefits: Weight-loss findings are modest and not a substitute for diet and activity.
safety: Can cause digestive upset and a fishy body odor.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: Green tea extract
benefits: Concentrated extract is not recommended here as a weight-loss strategy.
safety: Associated with liver injury, especially concentrated products; caffeine may add stimulant effects.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: Electrolyte mix
benefits: Can replace fluid-related electrolyte losses during prolonged, sweaty activity.
safety: Sodium and potassium need individual care with kidney, heart or blood-pressure conditions.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: Carbohydrate drink mix
benefits: Can supply carbohydrate during prolonged exercise when food is impractical.
safety: Count its calories; ordinary sessions may not require it.
how: Follow the product label and clinician advice. No blanket dosage is provided.

name: Beetroot / nitrate
benefits: May help some endurance exercise outcomes.
